features.summary: A view's plan: started in the view with the view's model, in a page, a partial, an editor template or a slot's content, and rendered at the view's end as a script of plan data; each view's plan is its own, nothing carries plan state between views on the server, and the plans of a page compose in the browser without merging, each with the owner whose container holds its script. The plan's types also hold a form's summary, refused for the container's block (N14.3); their plugin registration, a validator's browser rules, a component joined to the plan and an app-level object's door are claimed by modules 13, 8, 12 and 25.

features.oracle: MVC's own partial rendering on both hosts: a partial view runs with its own model and ViewData, rendered for a member under that member's TemplateInfo prefix (probe:core-template-prefix-name, probe:mvc5-template-full-id), and a partial's @section is dropped (probe:core-partial-section-dropped, probe:mvc5-sections-checked-in-layouts-only); and the HTML Standard, under which a script element of type application/json is a data block the browser never runs.

defects.defect: A plan rendered twice, so every handler it holds runs twice, a behavior written to a plan after it rendered, which the page never runs, or a plan a view opens and never renders, whose handlers the page never holds: a view renders the plan it opens once, after every door that takes it (D14.7, N14.2), and the plan analyzer refuses each at build (N18.15). The redesign refuses the first two where the view renders (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Document/PlanBuildContext.cs:52-57, Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Document/PlanBuildContext.cs:68-75), and main renders whatever the plan holds when RenderPlan runs (Alis.Reactive/Razor/Extensions/PlanExtensions.cs:113).

Each view's plan is its own (D14.1) and plans compose without merging (D14.2): a partial starts its plan with the one plan door, a container renders its own summary, and a view reaches another view's input by the member it binds, whose id is one in every view (D14.3).

features.summary: A slot: an element a plan loads into with a request's Into or empties with Unload, named in the plan by its id. A load replaces its content and an unload empties it; before either, the slot releases every owner inside its content, innermost first, then itself, each in D12.4's closed order and past a throw, and the step that asked stops with one error when a release threw. Content the server rendered inside a slot's container belongs to that slot, a loaded plan belongs to the innermost slot around its script, a load runs the content's own scripts and reads its plans before it releases, a step that writes over a slot of its own plan is refused, and a slot's plan listens to a component the page rendered through that component's id until the slot unloads.

meanings.meaning: A load runs each script its content holds, other than a plan's, once and in document order, after the content has replaced the slot's and before the content is mounted and its owner starts (D12.3, D12.4); a plan's script is its plan, read and never run. Fragment parsing marks every script it creates as already started, so content set as HTML runs none of them, while the same partial rendered with the page runs its scripts as the parser meets them: a vendor's helper that writes the script that builds its widget works in a slot as it does on the page. An inserted script that throws is reported by the browser and throws to no one, as D12.4 states for the content's replacement.

A load reads every plan its content holds before it releases anything. Content that holds a plan whose JSON does not parse, or that holds no number version or another version (D19.10, M14.D1), stops the step with one error naming the slot, before the release, so the slot keeps its content, its owner and their listeners, and the steps after it run nothing. The loaded body is data the network brought, a real boundary, and a slot left half replaced would hold content with no owner.

features.oracle: The DOM Standard's dispatch, whose inner invoke reports a listener's exception and runs the next listener (DOM Standard 2.9), and the HTML Standard: fragment parsing marks each script it creates as already started, so innerHTML runs none, a script element inserted by the DOM runs once, and custom element reactions are invoked with report (HTML Standard 4.13.6).

defects.defect: Content a load puts in a slot runs none of its scripts, since fragment parsing marks each as already started, so a widget its vendor's script builds stays unbuilt in a slot while the same partial builds it on the page; or a script runs again at each later load of other content (M9.D1). Main runs them only through Syncfusion's append, which evaluates the scripts when its third argument is true, and only when the page holds Syncfusion (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/execution/partials/inject.ts:31-36 at 623dd4a27).

Loaded content that holds another slot's container with content the server rendered in it gives that content's plan to the slot it was loaded into, so the inner slot's first load or unload releases nothing and the plan's handlers run until the outer slot unloads (D12.1, D12.3). The redesign starts every plan of loaded content under the loaded slot (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plugins/slot.ts:30, Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plugins/slot.ts:39 at 65fdf118d).

Loaded content holding a plan whose JSON does not parse releases the slot and replaces its content before the plan is read, so the slot shows half loaded content with no owner, or the step goes on as if it loaded (M9.D2).

A load or an unload of a slot whose element the page lacks, since it left with the slot around it, goes on as if it ran, or stops more than its own pipeline: it stops its own pipeline, as a missing element stops an element step's, and every other handler runs on (D10.21, D4.8).

An input a slot's content renders inside a request container is left out of the container: its rule is not checked with the container's, or its value is not sent with it. The 798 views of af5ad37a9 prove a slot's input and a cascade apart, on pages of their own, and none together (the owner, 2026-11-18: "Go build an app which involves partial views, conditional partial loading, independent partial loading. That is the main framework feature"). On the arrival desk the room a ward's partial renders is checked and sent as the page's own inputs are.

A partial a pipeline loads only when its condition holds stays outside the check of the container it is loaded into, so a rule that reads its input passes with the input empty. On the arrival desk the funding partial is loaded when Publicly funded is ticked, and the rule on its number, itself under the condition that the box is ticked, is held with the container's.

A partial a condition unloads leaves its input, or the rule on it, behind: the box stays on the page, or the container still asks for what no box holds. On the arrival desk, when Publicly funded is ticked off, the funding partial leaves arrival-funding and the arrival is recorded.

A partial that holds a container, a request and a validator of its own is checked by the page's rules, or the page by its: a save of one is refused for what the other lacks. On the arrival desk the next of kin partial's save is checked by its own two rules alone, and the arrival's rules by the arrival's request alone.

A cascade's list is loaded without the parents chosen before it or the care level read beside them, or a choice among a loaded list moves the saved draft: on the move-in, apartment 7 offers no bed, Willow offers apartment 9 under Assisted care, or the saved location changes with no save (MI.1, situation 1).

A cascade's first level left empty still sends its lookup, or leaves the levels under it on the page: on the move-in, an empty Community sends a second buildings GET, or the Building list stays (MI.1, situation 2).

A slot's load the server refuses by a status its request names runs the load, or no route: on the move-in, choosing a building the world holds closed shows no reason, or loads a list (MI.1, situation 3).

A slot's load whose connection drops on every attempt leaves the page with no word of it, or with choices it did not load: on the move-in, the failed apartments GET shows no notice, or an Apartment list (MI.1, situation 4).

A cascade's older answer, arriving after a newer choice replaced its run, loads its list over the newer one, or a lookup moves the saved draft before a save: on the move-in, Harbor House's late buildings stand over Maple Court's, or Saved location moves with no save (MI.1, situation 5).

A slot's load chosen among several by a condition loads another level's content, or a save keeps the content the load replaced: on the move-in, confirming Memory care shows another level's questions, or the saved draft still holds Assisted's answers (MI.2, situation 1).

A question a person declines still replaces a slot's content, or leaves the input that asked showing the level it did not load: on the move-in, No to Replace the current care answers? loads Memory's questions, or leaves Memory checked over Assisted's answers (MI.2, situation 2).

A slot's load the server refuses after its slot was unloaded shows no reason, or loads content, or moves the saved draft: on the move-in, Memory care refused by the server shows no message, or the saved care changes (MI.2, situation 3).

A slot's load whose connection drops on every attempt, after its slot was unloaded, leaves the page with no word of it or with content it did not load, or loses the saved content: on the move-in, the failed questions GET shows no notice, or the page opened again lacks Assisted's saved answers (MI.2, situation 4).

A slot's older load, answered after a newer choice replaced its run, puts its content over the newer one, and a save then holds both: on the move-in, Memory's late questions stand over Skilled's (MI.2, situation 5).

A reply read members deep shows another value or none, or a request its condition guards leaves where the condition fails: on the move-in, the identity check names nobody, or asks for a receipt the reply does not require (MI.3, situation 1).

A two-member rule over inputs of two attached partials passes where the members differ, in a pipeline's check of the container or in a request's rule set: on the move-in, a mismatched email confirmation is called ready, or its identity review leaves the page (MI.3, situation 2).

A refusal the server alone decides, answered by a status the request names with a typed body, runs the success route or no route: on the move-in, a resident who already holds an admission is called checked, or no reason shows (MI.3, situation 3).
A POST whose connection drops is sent again, or its failure shows no notice: on the move-in, the dropped identity review leaves twice, or the page says nothing (MI.3, situation 4).

A request under an awaited condition leaves before the condition's answer arrives, or a reply read members deep writes another value into a component: on the move-in, the allocation review is posted while readiness is still asked, or the panel shows another status or community (MI.4, situation 1).
An awaited condition nested under a condition that fails is still asked: on the move-in, an allocation panel that is not ready still asks the server for readiness (MI.4, situation 2).

A fallback for a value that reads nothing is not applied, or a conflict's body read members deep shows nobody: on the move-in, a bed taken since it was listed shows no holder, or a review reference of no text (MI.4, situation 3).
A run whose awaited method rejects goes on to the steps after it: on the move-in, a readiness call that never answers still writes the allocation line or posts a review (MI.4, situation 4).

A run a newer event replaced while it awaited a method goes on when its answer arrives: on the move-in, the review of an older bed selection posts a second review once its readiness answers (MI.4, situation 5).

promises.page: The move-in of draft D100, saved at version 7 for Helen Ward with bed BED4 at revision 12. Beside its request container move-in a partial of its own model renders the allocation panel, a ConformanceComponent whose inner text is North allocation desk and whose check POSTs the draft's readiness endpoint, and at its start GETs its desk, a partial of its own model, into allocation-desk. The desk's Review allocation runs a handler, under replace, that reads the container's bed and the panel's Check() in one condition and, where both hold, the panel's awaited SettleCheck() in a condition of its own; where that answers true it POSTs the allocation review as JSON, the location, the level, the resident and the version read from the container, Ready true and the panel's inner text as its reference. Its 200 sets the panel's Text to the status and its WriteOnlyText to the community's name, writes the allocation line and, where the reply's instructions are required, GETs them into allocation-instructions; its 409 writes who holds the bed, the review reference read from the container through IfNull, and whether a waitlist place is offered; where either condition fails it writes Allocation is not ready. Bed on file and the list Allocation reviews are what the page renders from the world's model.
